answer: For a summit poll on a basalt sculpture with a ripple motif, a registrar posts a $1,000 bond and publishes election-bound ID-to-key assignments. The server checks assignments and election-bound ballot signatures, counting one ballot per assigned ID and rejecting failures or repeats. Anyone may submit two registrar-signed assignments of different keys to one ID; officials verify them and forfeit the bond if both match this election. Shared keys enable abuse, and published IDs sacrifice privacy.
